'''John Lynch Phillips''' (born April 15, 1951) is a [[NASA]] [[astronaut]]. Phillips is also a [[Naval Aviator]] and retired [[Captain (naval)|captain]], [[United States Navy Reserve]]. Phillips has received numerous awards and special honors. He is a [[National Merit Scholar]], graduated 2nd in his class of 906 people at the [[U.S. Naval Academy]] in 1972. Phillips has also been awarded the [[NASA Space Flight Medal]], [[NASA Distinguished Service Medal]], the Gagarin Medal and several others. Phillips has logged over 4,400 flight hours and 250 aircraft carrier landings, flying the [[A-7 Corsair II]] carrier-based light attack aircraft while on active duty in the Regular Navy and subsequently during his time as a Navy Reservist from 1982 to 2002. At the time of his retirement, Phillips had retained the rank of captain.

==Biography==
Born April 15, 1951, in [[Fort Belvoir, Virginia]], but considers [[Scottsdale, Arizona]] to be his hometown. He is married to the former Laura Jean Doell of [[Scotia, New York]]. They have two children.

He graduated from [[Scottsdale High School]], [[Scottsdale, Arizona]], in 1966. He received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[mathematics]] and [[Russian (language)|Russian]] from the [[United States Naval Academy]] in 1972; a [[Master of Science]] degree in aeronautical systems from the [[University of West Florida]] in 1974; a Master of Science degree and a doctorate in geophysics and space physics from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 1984 and 1987 respectively.

A [[National Merit Scholar]]; he graduated second of 906 in the class of 1972 at U.S. Naval Academy; received 2 NASA Group Achievement Awards for contributions to the [[Ulysses probe|Ulysses Spacecraft Mission]] and the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] Distinguished Performance Award in 1996. Awarded the NASA Space Flight Medal and various military awards.

Phillips received a commission as an [[Ensign (rank)|ensign]] in the [[U.S. Navy]] upon graduation from the [[U.S. Naval Academy]] in 1972 and was designated a [[Naval Aviator]] in November 1974, concurrent with his completion of an MS degree in aeronautical systems from the [[University of West Florida]]. He trained in the [[A-7 Corsair]] aircraft at [[Naval Air Station Lemoore]], [[California]] and made overseas deployment with [[Second VA-155 (U.S. Navy)|Attack Squadron 155 (VA-155)]] aboard the [[aircraft carrier]]s {{USS|Oriskany|CV-34|6}} and {{USS|Franklin D. Roosevelt|CV-42|6}}. Subsequent tours of duty included Navy Recruiting Command duty in [[Albany, New York]], and flying the [[CT-39 Sabreliner]] aircraft at [[Naval Air Station North Island]], California.

After leaving the Regular Navy and transferring to the Naval Reserve in 1982, Phillips enrolled as a graduate student at UCLA. While at UCLA he carried out research involving observations by the NASA [[Pioneer Venus Spacecraft]]. Upon completing his doctorate in 1987, he was awarded a J. Robert Oppenheimer Postdoctoral Fellowship at Los Alamos National Laboratory in [[New Mexico]]. He accepted a career position at Los Alamos in 1989. While there, Phillips performed research on the sun and the space environment. From 1993 through 1996 he was Principal Investigator for the Solar Wind Plasma Experiment aboard the Ulysses Spacecraft as it executed a unique trajectory over the poles of the sun. He has authored 156 scientific papers dealing with the [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] environments of the sun, earth, other planets, comets and spacecraft.

Phillips has logged over 4,400 flight hours and 250 carrier landings. He was a Navy Reservist from 1982 to 2002, serving as an A-7 pilot, and in various non-flying assignments. He holds the rank of captain, USN (retired).<ref name=nasabio/>

== NASA ==
Selected by NASA in April 1996, Phillips reported to the [[Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center|Johnson Space Center]] in August 1996. After completing astronaut candidate training, he held various jobs in the Astronaut Office, including systems engineering and CAPCOM for the [[International Space Station]] (ISS). He served as a backup crew-member for ISS [[Expedition 7]].

===Spaceflight experience===
[[Image:ISS-11 Phillips at EVA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Attired in a Russian [[Orlan space suit|Orlan spacesuit]], Phillips participates in a [[extra-vehicular activity|spacewalk]].]]

'''[[STS-100]] ([[Space Shuttle Endeavour]], April 19 to May 1, 2001).'''<br />
STS-100 was a 12-day mission to the ISS. During the mission, the crew successfully delivered and installed the [[Mobile Servicing System|Canadarm2]] Robotic Arm. They also delivered experiments and supplies aboard the [[Multi-Purpose Logistics Module]] Raffaello on its maiden flight. Phillips was the Ascent/Entry Flight engineer and was the intravehicular activity coordinator during two spacewalks.

'''[[Expedition 11]] (April 15 to October 11, 2005).'''<br />
Expedition 11 was a six-month mission to the ISS.<br />
On April 15, 2005, Phillips, along with his fellow crew-members [[Sergei Krikalev]], and [[Roberto Vittori]] launched to the ISS aboard [[Soyuz TMA-6]].<br />
On June 14, 2005, Phillips became the first person to testify before Congress from the ISS, or [[outer space]] in general. He gave testimony to the [[United States House of Representatives]] [[Science Space Subcommittee]] via a live video feed. The hearing was to evaluate the space station's usefulness as an orbiting laboratory.<br />
On August 18, 2005, Phillips and Krikalev completed a five-hour spacewalk to retrieve several experiments and install a video camera for the new docking procedure.<br />
Phillips and Krikalev, along with Space Flight Participant [[Gregory Olsen]], returned to Earth aboard Soyuz TMA-6 on October 11, 2005.

'''[[STS-119]] ([[Space Shuttle Discovery]], March 15 to 28, 2009).'''<br />
STS-119 was a 12-day mission to the ISS flown during March 2009. It delivered and assembled the fourth starboard [[Integrated Truss Structure#P6, S6 trusses|Integrated Truss Segment (S6)]], and the fourth set of solar arrays and batteries to the station. The launch took place on March 15, 2009. Discovery successfully landed on March 28, 2009.<ref name=nasabio>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/phillips_john.pdf |title=NASA Bio JOHN L. PHILLIPS (PH.D.), NASA ASTRONAUT (FORMER) | publisher=NASA |date=August 2011 |access-date=May 15, 2021}}</ref>

Phillips was detailed to the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey, California, from 2009 to 2011 as the Smith/McCool NASA Chair Professor.
